questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) What is an operating system? (2 marks)

(b) State and describe TWO functions of an Operating system. (2 marks)

(c) Why are some operating system said to be mono-tasking? Give an example. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Operating system (2 marks).** An operating system (OS) is **system software** that manages the hardware and the software resources of a computer (processor, memory, storage, input/output devices), provides a **user interface**, and supplies the platform on which the application programs run. Examples: Windows, Linux, macOS, Android.

**(b) Two functions (2 marks)** (any two):

- **Memory management:** the OS allocates the main memory to the programs that need it, keeps the programs from overwriting each other and frees the memory when a program ends (it may use virtual memory).
- **File management:** it organises the files and folders on the storage devices, and creates, names, copies, deletes and protects them.
- **Process (processor) management:** it decides which program uses the processor and for how long (scheduling).
- **Device management:** it controls the input and output devices through device drivers.
- **Security and user management:** it controls the user accounts, passwords and access rights.

**(c) Mono-tasking (2 marks).** A mono-tasking (single-tasking) operating system can run **only one program at a time**: the next program can start only after the current one has finished, because the OS has no scheduler to share the processor and the memory among several programs (it was designed for simple computers with little memory and a single user). *Example:* **MS-DOS**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain the following terms in project management:

(a) Task. (1 mark)

(b) Slack task. (1 mark)

(c) Critical path. (2 marks)

(d) PERT chart. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Task (1 mark).** A **single, well-defined activity or piece of work** in a project that has a duration, needs resources and must be completed (for example "install the network cables").

**(b) Slack task (1 mark).** A task that is **not on the critical path**: it has **slack (float) time**, meaning that it can start late or take longer by that amount of time **without delaying the end of the whole project**.

**(c) Critical path (2 marks).** The **longest sequence of dependent tasks** from the start to the end of the project. Its length gives the **shortest possible duration of the project**; the tasks on it have **zero slack**, so a delay in any one of them delays the whole project and they need the closest control.

**(d) PERT chart (2 marks).** PERT (*Program Evaluation and Review Technique*) chart: a **network diagram** that shows the tasks of a project as arrows or boxes, with their **durations** and their **dependencies** (which task must finish before another can start). It is used to plan and schedule the project, to find the earliest and latest start times, the critical path and the slack of each task.

*Example (checked by a script).* Tasks: A (3 days, first), B (2 days, after A), C (4 days, after A), D (1 day, after B and C).

| Task | Duration | Earliest start | Earliest finish | Latest finish | Slack |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 3 | 0 | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| B | 2 | 3 | 5 | 7 | 2 |
| C | 4 | 3 | 7 | 7 | 0 |
| D | 1 | 7 | 8 | 8 | 0 |

The critical path is A - C - D (3 + 4 + 1 = 8 days). B is a slack task: it can be delayed by 2 days without delaying the project.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain the functions of the following stating an appropriate example.

(a) ISP. (2 marks)

(b) Protocol. (1 mark)

(c) Handshaking. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) ISP (2 marks).** An *Internet Service Provider* is a company that **gives customers access to the Internet** (usually for a subscription), assigns them an IP address, and often provides services such as e-mail accounts, web hosting and DNS. *Example:* CAMTEL, MTN Cameroon or Orange Cameroon.

**(b) Protocol (1 mark).** A **set of agreed rules** that defines how data is formatted, addressed, sent, received and checked for errors, so that different devices and programs can communicate with one another. *Example:* HTTP (web pages), SMTP (sending e-mail), TCP/IP (the Internet).

**(c) Handshaking (2 marks).** The **exchange of signals between two devices before the real data transfer** to establish the connection and to agree on the parameters of the communication (speed, data format, error checking), and to show that each side is ready. *Example:* in TCP, the three-way handshake SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK before a web page is sent; or a modem and a computer agreeing on a transmission speed.
